name: January 26, 2022 - Regular Meeting
agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID19
and pursuant to the AB361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order (revised
January 10, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and
the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting .

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bayala@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well as
states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, State of California, and a federal
emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in person
would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This way, the public, the staff, and the
Council will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.
Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests
that you sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Mayor and then you must be
 Public Works Commission  Page 3 of 3  January 26, 2022

present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions
for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the Public Works Department, and available upon request by emailing bayala@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 21st day of January 2022, at 1:00 p.m.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve minutes of the Public Works Commission Special

DISCUSSION: Staff has prepared draft minutes for the Public Works Commission Special
meeting December 14, 2021, and hereby submits the minutes for Commission approval.

ATTACHMENTS:

1. Draft Minutes of December 14, 2021, Public Works Commission Special meeting

  Page 1 of 1
  Agenda Item # 2.B.1.
   MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC WORKS COMMISSION
  SPECIAL MEETING
  DECEMBER 14, 2021
  TELECONFERENCED – VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  4:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-08-21 and
fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19)
pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Simmens called the meeting to order at 4:06 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Lance Simmens; Vice Chair Wade Major; and Commissioners Scott
  Dittrich, Brian Merrick and James Palmer

  ALSO PRESENT:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Troy Spayd, Assistant Public
  Works Director; Travis Hart, Public Works Superintendent; Julie Santia, Associate Civil
  Engineer; Jenna Sobieray, Associate Civil Engineer; Mary Linden, Executive Assistant;
  Parker Davis, Media Technician; and Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Simmens led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Palmer moved, and Commissioner Dittrich seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Senior Administrative Assistant Ayala reported that the agenda for the meeting was
  properly posted on December 10, 2021.

ITEM 1.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM 1.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Works Superintendent Hart provided an update on today’s storm event. He
  discussed the City’s response to a wind event in late November.
 Malibu Public Works Commission
Special Meeting
Minutes of December 14, 2021
Page 2 of 5
_________________________

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated there was a transformer explosion in front of
  the Civic Center Water Treatment Facility (CCWTF) today. He stated the CCWTF
  emergency generators functioned properly and there were no issues at the facility.
  He stated he contacted Caltrans about failure of battery backups on some traffic
  signals today. He announced a joint meeting with the Public Safety Commission
  would be scheduled to discuss Measure R and Measure M projects, as well as the
  Westward Beach project, as directed by the City Council at its December 13, 2021
  meeting. He introduced Associate Civil Engineer Julie Santia.

ITEM 1.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Commissioner Palmer requested an update on the broken drain. Public Works
  Director DuBoux stated Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian had been in
  contact with Caltrans to fix its broken drain. Commissioner Palmer asked if utilities
  could be undergrounded in the open trench of the signal synchronization project.
  Public Works Director DuBoux stated it was not in the scope of work for the
  project. Commissioner Palmer suggested Malibu become a green city by adding
  composting. Executive Assistant Linden stated she would send information from
  the Environmental Programs office about a composting program.

  Vice Chair Major stated he witnessed the transformer explosion in front of the
  CCWTF today. He discussed the economic cost of power outages due to failing
  Southern California Edison (SCE) infrastructure. He stated SCE should not be
  publicly held and own all the infrastructure.

  Commissioner Dittrich agreed with Vice Chair Major. He stated the City should
  work with SCE to underground utilities when opportunities exist from other
  projects.

  Chair Simmens commended Public Works Director DuBoux and Commissioner
  Dittrich for their presentations to the City Council resulting in the Westward Beach
  project coming back to the Commission. He discussed the Thanksgiving power
  outages. He stated long-term alternatives should be discussed. He stated parking,
  composting, and undergrounding should be added to the Commission’s work plan.

  Senior Administrative Assistant Ayala confirmed the Joint Special meeting with
  the Public Safety Commission would be held on January 19, 2022 at 6:00 p.m.

ITEM 2  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Dittrich moved, and Commissioner Palmer seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  1.  Approval of Minutes – October 27, 2021

ITEM 3  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 4  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Capital Improvement Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects Status Report
  Staff recommendation: Receive and file report on the status of the City’s current
  and upcoming Capital Improvements Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects.

  Assistant Public Works Director Spayd and Public Works Superintendent Hart
  presented the report.

  Vice Chair Major commended staff on the Civic Center Way improvements. He
  asked if the Commission would get to review the Caltrans plans for median
  improvements. Public Works Director DuBoux stated it would delay the project but
  could be looked at for a future project.

  In response to Vice Chair Major, Public Works Director DuBoux suggested
  members of both the Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
  make site visits to Westward Beach before the joint meeting. Vice Chair Major
  requested staff provide a map showing agency jurisdiction.

  In response to Vice Chair Major, Assistant Public Works Director Spayd discussed
  minor changes to the design of the permanent skate park.

  Commissioner Dittrich requested the existing plan for Westward Beach be
  distributed. In response to Commissioner Dittrich, Assistant Public Works Director
  Spayd stated changes to the crosswalk at Nobu were part of the PCH
  synchronization project and would be reviewed by the Planning Commission.

  B.  Los Angeles County Measure R and M Transportation Funding Update
  Staff recommendation: 1) Receive an update on Los Angeles County Measure R
  and Measure M Transportation Funding; and 2) Identify projects to improve safety
  on Pacific Coast Highway and canyon roads using Los Angeles County Measure R
  and Measure M transportation funds.
 Malibu Public Works Commission
Special Meeting
Minutes of December 14, 2021
Page 4 of 5
_________________________

  Public Works Director DuBoux provided a presentation with the report. He
  discussed a few potential new projects that have been mentioned. He stated he
  hoped to get a priority list from the Joint Special meeting of the Public Works
  Commission and Public Safety Commission to present to the City Council.

  In response to Commissioner Palmer, Public Works Director DuBoux discussed
  how priorities were established in the PCH Safety Study. He stated those priorities
  could be reevaluated.

  Commissioner Dittrich asked problems were solved by the raised medians. Public
  Works Director DuBoux stated the medians prevented unsafe U-turns. He
  confirmed traffic data identified areas where those unsafe turns resulted in
  accidents. Commissioner Dittrich suggested extending the right turn lane from
  westbound PCH at Webb Way. Public Works Director DuBoux stated that could
  be considered. Commissioner Dittrich discussed light pollution from beacon signs.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated changes to projects not yet started could be
  made prior to presenting the funding agreement to Metro.

  Commissioner Merrick stated the Paradise Cove intersection was a choke point in
  the summer. He suggested adding a right-hand turn into Paradise Cove eastbound
  and lengthening the left hand turn on westbound PCH. He stated the Sheriff’s
  Department had requested improvements at El Matador Beach during the PCH
  Safety Study discussions.

  Vice Chair Major agreed with Commissioner Merrick’s suggestions. He stated the
  priority list addressed many of the biggest problem spots in the City. In response to
  Vice Chair Major, Public Works Director DuBoux stated the improvements near
  Moonshadows did not include a crosswalk. He suggested LED lights be added to
  crosswalks instead of a beacon.

  Commissioner Dittrich stated the Las Flores Canyon Road and Rambla Vista area
  was the number one problem area identified in the PCH Safety Study. He discussed
  rocks falling in Malibu Canyon by the tunnel. He suggested considering adding
  netting to stop the rocks. Public Works Director DuBoux stated he would discuss
  with the COG Executive Director how to get the County to add that to its identified
  projects in Malibu Canyon. Commissioner Dittrich suggested extending the left
  turn lane from eastbound PCH onto Cross Creek Road.

  Vice Chair Major asked if there were other, less light-intensive technologies
  available as alternates to beacons that could be activated only when a pedestrian
  wanted to cross.

  Chair Simmens suggested adding bicycle lane striping. He stated the primary need
  was to separate cars from the cyclists.

  C.  Mid-Year Report to the City Council
  Staff recommendation: Develop a list of the Commission’s activities for the period
  of July through December 2021 to be included in the Interim City Manager’s Mid-
  Year Commission Activity Report, scheduled to be presented to the City Council
  at its Regular meeting on January 24, 2022.

  Senior Administrative Assistant Ayala presented the report.

MOTION  Commissioner Palmer moved, and Vice Chair Major seconded a motion to approve
  the list of the Commission’s activities for the period of July through December
  2021 to be included in the Interim City Manager’s Commission Activity Report,
  scheduled to be presented to the City Council at its Regular meeting on January 24,
  2022. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 5:34 p.m., Chair Simmens adjourned the meeting.

  Approved and adopted by the Public Works Commission of the City
  of Malibu on January 26, 2022.

Subject:  Capital Improvement Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects Status

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file report on the status of the City’s current and
upcoming Capital Improvements Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects.

DISCUSSION: Staff will provide a status update on the following active projects in the
Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Capital Improvement Program:

  anticipated to have a final design by March 2022. The project will be
  advertised for construction bids shortly after this date.
   Project Schedule:
   Complete Design: March 2022
   Begin Construction: Spring 2022

PCH Median Improvements Project
   Updates:
   The project was approved by the Planning Commission on September
  8, 2021. This project requires Caltrans approval since the work will be
  on Pacific Coast Highway. The project reports and plans are being
  routed through Caltrans for final approval. It is anticipated that the
  project will have final approval by March 2022. The project will be

   advertised for construction bids after this date. A construction manager
  agreement will be sent to City Council in March.
   Project Schedule:
   Complete Design: March 2022
   Begin Construction: Spring/Summer 2022

PCH Signal Synchronization System Improvements Project
   Updates:
   This project will be presented to the Planning Commission in February
  2022. This project requires Caltrans approval since the work will be on
  PCH. The project reports and plans are being routed through Caltrans
  for final approval. It is anticipated that the project will have final
  approval by March 2022. The project will be advertised for construction
  bids shortly after final approval. If possible, the construction of this
  project will begin in conjunction with the PCH Median Improvement
  Project Schedule:
   Complete Final Design: Spring 2022
   Advertise: Spring/Summer 2022
   Award Contract and Begin Construction: Spring/Summer 2022

Westward Beach Road Improvements Project
   Updates:
   The design plans were approved by Planning Commission on
  September 20, 2021. At the December 13, 2021, City Council meeting,
  Council directed staff to withdraw the proposed project and associated
  Coastal Development Permit and directed the Public Works and Public
  Safety Commissions to review the project to develop project
  alternatives. A joint Public Works and Public Safety Commission
  meeting was held on January 20, 2022. Project alternatives will be
  presented to the commissions at a future date.
   Project Schedule:
   Complete Design: Spring 2022
   Begin Construction: Summer/Winter 2022

Civic Center Water Treatment Facility Phase 2
   Updates:
   Individual letters were mailed to all properties within Phase 2 with their
  preliminary estimated assessments. Staff has been communicating
  with the property owners regarding their proposed assessments.
   The MOU has been amended modifying the deadline to the formation
  of the assessment district to June 30, 2022.
   Staff mailed easement documents to property owners for review and
  execution in July and has followed up with an additional letter to those
  property owners.

    Project Schedule:
   Complete Design: December 2021
   Advertise for Bidding: February 2022
   Begin Construction: Fall 2022

Bluffs Park Shade Structure
   Project Description: This project consists of the installation of four single-post
  shade structures at Malibu Bluffs Park.
   Updates:
   Staff is currently working on the design of the project and anticipates
  sending this project out to bid during the Spring of 2022.
   Estimated Schedule:
   Complete Design: Spring 2022
   Begin Construction: Spring 2022

Permanent Skate Park
   Project Description: This project includes the designing and constructing a
  permanent skate park located on the Crummer/Case Court parcel adjacent
  to Malibu Bluffs Park. The project would include parking and additional site
  amenities such as trash cans, benches, tables, and restrooms.
   Updates:
   In May 2021, the Council approved funding for additional engineering
  work related to the project. Staff has worked with the consultant over
  the past several months to complete the engineering work, and the final
  draft plans are expected to be completed in early 2022. The Planning
  Commission will then review the project in Spring 2022 before final
  review by the Council.
   Estimated Schedule:
   Complete Design: Spring 2022
   Begin Construction: To be determined

PCH at Trancas Canyon Road Right Turn Lane
   Project Description: This project consists of installing a new westbound right
  turn lane at the intersection of PCH and Trancas Canyon Road.
   Updates:
   Staff is reviewing the submitted proposals and will select a qualified
  consultant. It is anticipated that this agreement will go to Council in
  March 2022
   Estimated Schedule:
   Begin Design: Spring 2022

Capital Improvement Projects (Construction)

The City does not have projects in construction at this time.

  Agenda Item # 4.A.
 Capital Improvement Projects (Not Started)

Vehicle Protection Devices
   Project Description: Per Malibu Municipal Code Section 17.48.070 requires
  vehicle impact protection devices to be installed for all parking spaces located
  adjacent to any outdoor pedestrian seating area. There are two locations
  within the City’s right-of-way and City-owned property that would require a
  vehicle impact protection device.

Legacy Park Paver Repair Project
   Project Description: This project will consist of removing and repairing a large
  section of pavers in Legacy Park. The pavers have become uneven and
  damaged in several areas

Malibu Bluffs Park South Walkway
   Project Description: This project will include replacing the existing sidewalk
  located on the south side of Malibu Bluffs Park.

Trancas Playground Resurfacing
   Project Description: The project will include removing and replacing the upper
  layer of the playground surfacing at Trancas Canyon Park.

PCH Median Improvements at Paradise Cove and Zuma Beach
   Project Description: This project was identified in the 2015 PCH Safety Study
  and includes installing new raised medians and improvements. New raised
  medians are proposed east and west of PCH and Paradise Cove Road. The
  proposed improvements also include the relocation of the existing bus stop
  and new signage. The project will also include the installation of new raised
  medians on PCH in the areas where the double yellow lines exist in the vicinity
  of Zuma Beach, specifically where the yellow paddles are installed.

Capital Improvement Projects (Completed)

Civic Center Way Improvements
   Updates: The contractor has completed the planting material maintenance
  period as described within the project documents. Council accepted this
  project as complete at the September 13th City Council Meeting.

Civic Center Stormwater Diversion Structure
   Updates: The contractor has completed the storm drain improvements in the
  Civic Center Way are. The improvements modified the existing concrete
  channel underneath Civic Center Way by adding a 3’ concrete curb adjacent
  to the existing flap gates. The new curb prevents brackish water intrusion

   into the City’s Civic Center Stormwater Treatment Facility. This project is
  scheduled to be accepted by the Council at the January 24, 2022 meeting.

2021 Annual Street Maintenance

Disaster Projects (Design)

  
Birdview Avenue Improvements (CalOES Project)

Malibu Park Drainage Improvements

  January 24, 2022 meeting.

Clover Heights Storm Drain (FEMA Project)
   Project Description: This project consists of design and construction of a few
  storm drains on Clover Heights. The existing storm drain facility ends at the
  intersection of Clover Heights and Harvester Road. During storms, this
  intersection floods and causes debris to block the road. An extended storm
  drain towards the end of Clover Heights will help eliminate this issue.
   Updates:
   Staff is currently preparing consultant proposals for the design of this
  project. Proposals will be due in February/March.

Latigo Canyon Road Culvert Repairs (FEMA Project)
   Project Description: This project consists of repairing the existing storm drain
  on Latigo Canyon Road located approximately 2,500 feet from PCH that was
  damaged by the Woolsey Fire.

  Agenda Item # 4.A.
    Updates:

   Updates:
   The project design will commence during the Spring 2022.
   Estimated Schedule: TBD

   Updates:
   The City has hired a consultant to design this project. The design has
  started and is anticipated to be completed by the Spring of 2022.
   Estimated Schedule:
   Complete Design: Spring 2022
   Begin Construction: Fall 2022

Westward Beach Road Shoulder Repairs (CalOES Project)
   Project Description: The project consists of repairs the damaged shoulder on
  Westward Beach Road.
   Upates:
   This project is currently under design with the City’s consultant. It is
  anticipated that the final design will be complete by July 2022. The
  project will be advertised for construction bids with construction
  beginning in Fall 2022.
   Estimated Schedule:
   Complete Design: July 2022
   Begin Construction: Fall 2022
  
Outdoor Warningn Sirens - Design (FEMA Project)
   Project Description: An Emergency Warning Siren system will improve the
  City’s ability to alert the community by providing mechanisms to alert
  residents in areas without power and those who live in neighborhoods with
  poor cell service. Phase One of the project included a sound study to
  determine the optimal number and locations of individual sirens, power and
  infrastructure requirements, and siren sound range. The City has been
  Page 7 of 8
  Agenda Item # 4.A.
   awarded a FEMA Hazard Mitigation grant to fund the design, engineering and
  environmental compliance needed for a shovel ready project. Phase Two of
  the Emergency Warning Sirens project will be implementation of the design
  plan, including purchasing, installing, and testing the sirens. The City will
  apply for future grant funding for this phase of the project.
   Upates:
   On November 30, 2021, City Council approved an agreement with
  Acoustic Technology to design the outdoor warning sirens. A design
  report will be presented to Council upon completion.
   Estimated Schedule: TBD

Disaster Projects (Construction)
None at this time

Disaster Projects (Completed)

Citywide Guardrail Replacement
Project Description: This project consisted of replacing the damaged guardrails throughout
the City caused by the Woolsey Fire on Encinal Canyon Road, Corral Canyon Road, and
Kanan Dume Road. The project was combined with the County of Los Angeles’ damaged
guardrails. The project was completed in February 2021.

Malibu Park Storm Drain Repairs
Project Description: After the Woolsey Fire, subsequent storms caused damage to
multiple storm drain facilities throughout Malibu. The project repaired the storm drains on
Cuthbert Road, Morning View Drive, Busch Drive at Harvester Road. The project also
included the repair of a storm drainage facility on Birdview Avenue.

MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC WORKS COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 26, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED – VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  3:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-08-21 and
fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19)
pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Simmens called the meeting to order at 3:32 p.m.
ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Lance Simmens; Vice Chair Wade Major; and Commissioners Scott
  Dittrich, and James Palmer

  ABSENT:  Commissioner Brian Merrick

  ALSO PRESENT:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Troy Spayd, Assistant Public
  Works Director; Travis Hart, Public Works Superintendent; Arthur Aladjadjian, Public
  Works Superintendent; Mary Linden, Executive Assistant; Parker Davis, Media
  Technician; and Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Dittrich led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Palmer moved, and Commissioner Dittrich seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Merrick absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Senior Administrative Assistant Ayala reported that the agenda for the meeting was
  properly posted on January 21, 2022.

ITEM 1.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.
 Malibu Public Works Commission
Special Meeting
Minutes of January 26, 2022
Page 2 of 4
_________________________

ITEM 1.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed the Joint Special meeting with the Public
  Safety Commission. He stated the consultant was working on exhibits related to
  alternative designs to be presented at the next Joint Special meeting to be held
  possibly the week of February 21. He stated any recommendations from the
  Commissions would be presented to the City Council. He stated Mayor Pro Tem
  Silverstein expressed support for Chair Simmens’ suggestions for improving PCH.
  He stated he was meeting tomorrow with a Congressional representative about
  possible additional available funding.

  Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian provided an update on mud flow and
  damages from the storms in early January. He stated he contacted the Caltrans
  Acting District Director for Maintenance.

  Commissioner Palmer stated both water and mud sheeted down onto Bayshore
  Drive, causing erosion and breaking a water line. Public Works Superintendent
  Aladjadjian discussed maintenance Los Angeles County Waterworks was doing on
  that line in weeks before it broke.

  Public Works Superintendent Hart discussed the status of debris cleanup in the
  canyons and berm repairs following the early January storms. He discussed
  damages from recent high winds. He announced striping work was scheduled next
  week on Kanan Dume Drive near the arrester bed.

ITEM 1.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Commissioner Dittrich discussed comments at the January 24, 2022 City Council
  meeting regarding signals not included in the PCH synchronization project. Public
  Works Director DuBoux confirmed that all signals from Topanga Canyon Road to
  John Tyler Drive would be connected. Commissioner Dittrich asked if utility
  undergrounding could be included in any PCH beautification project.

  Chair Simmens stated undergrounding utilities as a pilot project could be included
  in his recommendations for a redesign of PCH. Public Works Director DuBoux
  agreed it could be included in the project proposal.

  Commissioner Palmer thanked Public Works Director DuBoux and Public Works
  Superintendent Aladjadjian for their assistance with the drainpipe problem. He
  stated composting would help the City be more green.

  Vice Chair Major commended staff for an excellent joint meeting. He stated
  overlapping jurisdictions in Malibu created problems and Caltrans was the weak
  link. He asked if there was any political solution for improving the relationship with
  Caltrans. Public Works Director DuBoux stated he was working hard to improve
 Malibu Public Works Commission
Special Meeting
Minutes of January 26, 2022
Page 3 of 4
_________________________

  his relationship with local directors. Vice Chair Major stated the City should be
  noticed before a project is approved. He suggested the City lobby to have the
  Caltrans structure changed to make it more efficient. Public Works Director
  DuBoux discussed how the City communicates with various levels within Caltrans.
  In response to Vice Chair Major, Public Works Director DuBoux discussed
  Caltrans’ role in undergrounding utilities on PCH.

  Chair Simmens stated it was most important to get the Secretary of Transportation’s
  support.

  Commissioner Dittrich discussed rocks and debris falling on Malibu Canyon Road.
  He suggested fencing be installed to prevent rocks from reaching the road. He
  discussed the need for California Highway Patrol (CHP) coverage on PCH.

  Chair Simmens thanked everyone for a good joint meeting. In response to Chair
  Simmens, Public Works Director DuBoux discussed the budget and work plan
  process. Chair Simmens stated parking issues needed to be included in the
  Commission’s work plan.

  Commissioner Palmer agreed the joint meeting was successful. He stated all
  comments received expressed opposition to the Westward Beach project.

  Chair Simmens stated the opposition was a coordinated effort. He stated the project
  required balance between public safety and environmental concerns.

ITEM 2  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Palmer moved, and Vice Chair Major seconded a motion to approve
  the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Merrick absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes – October 27, 2021
  Staff recommendation: Approve minutes of the Public Works Commission
  Special meeting October 27, 2021.

ITEM 3  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 4  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Capital Improvement Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects Status Report
  Staff recommendation: Receive and file report on the status of the City’s current
  and upcoming Capital Improvements Projects and Disaster Recovery Projects.

  Assistant Public Works Director Spayd thanked Task Force Member Dittrich for
  his comments in support of staff at the City Council meeting. He agreed with
  Commissioner Dittrich’s comments about safety concerns on Malibu Canyon Road.
  He presented the report on Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) and Disaster
  Projects in design. He stated staff had begun work on the five-year CIP plan and a
  storm drain master plan.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated he provided a CIP update to Council at a
  recent meeting. He stated the five-year plan was a tool for identifying and managing
  future projects.

  Commissioner Palmer asked if there were timelines for using Measure R or
  Measure M funds before the funding was lost. Public Works Director DuBoux
  explained the process for funding approval.

  Vice Chair Major discussed three projects related to Trancas Canyon Park. He
  suggested they be done together, if possible. Public Works Director DuBoux stated
  the complexity of projects required them to be separate.

  In response to Commissioner Dittrich, Public Works Director DuBoux stated he
  would forward the spreadsheet of projects for prioritization next week.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 4:26 p.m., Chair Simmens adjourned the meeting.

  Approved and adopted by the Public Works Commission of the City
  of Malibu on March 23, 2022.

  ___________________________
